Long-running coroutine that receives Cmd values (Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Restart) and owns the live Claude process.
It spawns the process lazily, respawns it when the rules version changes, and resumes the stored session id.
A generation counter drops events from killed processes.
Streamed events become chat items; file-touching tool results bump repo_version and reload the open file, and Done finishes the current graph job.
Every delivered message outside a job starts a chat turn in app-state, which Done settles against the baseline.
Changing a project's repositories or descriptions also restarts Claude with the updated project context.

Long-running coroutine that receives Cmd values (Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Restart) and owns the live Claude process.
It spawns the process lazily, respawns it when the rules version changes, and resumes the stored session id.
A generation counter drops events from killed processes.

title: Node history
before:
Title: Node history
Kind: store
Links: git-service, graph-model, workbench-files
Files:
  src/node_history.rs
  src/state.rs
  src/git.rs

Shared, append-only history of node and module changes (title, kind, module, reference, links, files and description) stored as before/after text.
Each entry has a unique id, a time, an author (git user.name) and a source: a person in Workbench, Claude working for that person, or an edit outside Workbench.
The log is .workbench/node-history.jsonl, one entry per line, with a .workbench/.gitattributes union-merge rule so logs from several people merge without conflicts; on load lines are de-duplicated by id and sorted by time.
What this client last saw of the graph is kept locally in ~/.config/workbench/node-snapshots/, and a change already in the shared log (for example pulled from a teammate) is not logged again.
Rapid edits by the same person are merged into one entry, and a built-in LCS line diff renders entries as classic +/− diffs.
